the topological charge of classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equation in the spherical ansatze is non-zero at finite order in perturbation theory in g and that it can be expressed as an analytic function of g.

we have developed a perturbative method to calculate the topological charge of classical SU(2) solutions in Minkowski spacetime, which is non-integer, and that we have calculated the first non-trivial order of this charge for specific solutions.

the topological charge Q can be expressed in a power series expansion of the gauge coupling g, which can be nonzero already at finite order, and that the order g5 term can be calculated explicitly for specific initial pulses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new type of classical solution to gauge field equations of motion, with non-integer topological charge, and that this charge is a non-perturbative effect.
the topological charge Q is not a gauge invariant observable in the classical limit.
we show that the perturbative expansion of a classical field theory can lead to non-integer topological charges.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topological charge is not necessarily quantised in a classical field theory.

the classical equations of a gauge theory, without the need to introduce any fermions or any Higgs fields, may give rise to a non-integer topological charge, and to anomalous fermion-number violation.
the topological charge of a classical gauge solution is not necessarily a conserved quantity, even in the absence of fermions, because it may depend non-perturbatively on the gauge coupling.
